article.title: No. 9 Texas Tech wants more than 10-win seasons with another Big 12 title game in reach vs. TCU
article.linkText: No. 9 Texas Tech wants more than 10-win seasons with another Big 12 title game in reach vs. TCU

categories.description: TCU Horned Frogs @ Texas Tech Red Raiders

event.description: TCU Horned Frogs @ Texas Tech Red Raiders

keywords: TCU Horned Frogs @ Texas Tech Red Raiders
article.story: LUBBOCK, Texas -- — No. 9 Texas Tech has already clinched consecutive 10-win seasons for the first time in school history, though that isn't how coach Joey McGuire views success for his Red Raiders a year after winning the Big 12 championship and making the College Football Playoff. “Success to me looks like going back to the Big 12 championship game, winning it and finding a way to win in the playoffs,” McGuire said this week. “It's going to look totally different than what I imagined in January what it would look like. But these guys have found a way.” The Red Raiders (10-1, 7-1 Big 12, No. 11 CFP) take a school-record 14-game home winning streak into Thursday night's game against TCU (5-6, 3-5), which just fired coach Sonny Dykes. Another win puts them in the conference championship game against No. 2 Utah (11-0, 8-0, No. 2 CFP) on Dec. 4, when the winner is guaranteed a spot in the 12-team playoff field. Texas Tech lost 23-0 loss to Oregon in the CFP quarterfinal at the Orange Bowl last year after a No. 4 final ranking and first-round bye. A loss to TCU wouldn’t immediately knock the Red Raiders out of the Big 12 title game, but they would then need Cincinnati to win at No. 11 BYU (9-2, 6-2, No. 10 CFP) on Saturday. The Cougars, last year's Big 12 runner-up, would own a tiebreaker based on records against five common league opponents since they didn’t play Tech this season. “We know that if we take care of business, we’re in the Big 12 championship,” McGuire said. “That’s helping us a little bit focus more on that.” Texas Tech has a four-game winning streak since its loss at Cincinnati on Oct. 24, and dual-threat quarterback Thomas Castellanos replaced Will Hammond as the starter. Touted transfer QB Brendan Sorsby went through spring practice with Tech before being ruled ineligible for gambling during his college career, and in June dropped his suit against the NCAA seeking to regain his eligibility. Frogs faced a short week after coaching change TCU plays four days after Dykes was fired. It lost 38-17 in the home finale to Utah, which after blowing a 17-0 halftime lead scored three touchdowns in the final 5:46. “We’re gonna get our minds right, we’re gonna keep the vibe right, we’re going to get to working,” said TCU interim head coach Andy Avalos, its third-year defensive coordinator and former Boise State head coach. “There’s unbelievable people in this building that are gonna lock arms, and we’re gonna move forward together and finish this thing right.” The Frogs could become the league's 11th bowl-eligible team. Red Raiders are running the ball J'Koby Williams has four consecutive 100-yard rushing games for Texas Tech, which has averaged 252.3 yards per game on the ground in that span. He is fourth in the Big 12 at 108.6 yards rushing per game, and ranks second in FBS with 7.5 yards per carry. The Red Raiders have averaged 40 points and 489 total yards in Castellanos' four starts, up for 36 points and 419 yards in their first seven games. The former Boston College and Florida State QB has 12 passing TDs and 18.4 yards per completion, FBS-bests in that span. “He’s really caught his rhythm," Avalos said. “Tip your hat to the coaches too. They’ve created a structure and put him in position with what they’re doing with their offense now." The sacks are still coming for Tech's defense The Red Raiders have 36 sacks, three more than at this point last year with six defensive players who were then NFL draft picks in April. Defensive tackle A.J. Holmes Jr., a second-team AP All-America pick last season when he had 4 1/2 of Tech's 41 sacks, is now the Big 12 leader. He has 10, and is the first interior linemen in school history to reach double figures in a season. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full college football coverage here
